newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon wraps up parliamentary election Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Gabon wraps up parliamentary election Sunday.

text.p: Gabon holds the second round of its parliamentary elections on Sunday with President Omar Bongo's ruling party on course for an outright majority.

Bongo's Democratic Party won 47 of the 55 national assembly seats decided in the December 15 first round and electoral officials say Bongo supporters take a lead into the run-offs for many of the undecided seats. The assembly has 120 seats.
"Everything is more than ready," Vincent Mintsa-Eya, a spokesman of the electoral commission told Reuters on Saturday.
The main opposition National Woodcutters Rally (RNB), which won control of the capital Libreville during chaotic October municipal elections, only managed three seats on December 15.

It and other opposition parties have called for the parliamentary results to be scrapped and the elections rerun. The opposition denounced problems with voter cards and electoral lists during the first round.
The elections are part of a democratic timetable brokered in Paris in 1994 after political violence shook the oil-producing Central African nation, killing more than a dozen people.
They are Gabon's second multiparty legislative polls. The first were in 1990 when a wave of democratic reform swept across Africa after the fall of Soviet-bloc communism.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of Gabon's founding head of state, Leon Mba.
